references.text: Pharaoh readies his chariot and takes his army with him, including six hundred chosen chariots with their commanders. This is the historical account of the army that later drowned.
The Egyptians pursued the Israelites into the sea with all Pharaoh's horses, chariots, and horsemen. This verse describes the event before the drowning.
The sea turned back and covered the chariots and horsemen and the entire army of Pharaoh that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Parallel account of the same event.
A hymn celebrating how the Lord shook Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds. Poetic retelling of the same event.
The sea closed over their enemies. A poetic reference to the destruction of the Egyptians in the sea.
The water covered their opponents; not one of them was left. Confirms that Pharaoh's entire army perished in the sea.
By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land, but when the Egyptians tried to do the same, they drowned. New Testament reference to the event at the Sea of Reeds.
Exodus 14:28 gives the concrete continuation of the judgment mentioned in Exodus 15:4.
Deuteronomy 11:4 confirms and applies the judgment over Egypt as a lasting lesson.
Exodus 15:19 highlights the contrast between Pharaoh's downfall and Israel's deliverance through the same event.
Joshua 24:6 confirms the story of the pursuit to the sea as the basis for God's salvation.
